target: Default Admin and shared Drupal interface review
automation: Proposed contracts only; not implemented scanner rules. No automatic enforcement.

rules.title: Compare equivalent contexts
rules.statement: Compare a component only within a declared theme, account, language, direction, viewport, state and preference context. Preserve unknown theme evidence.
rules.check: Record actual, configured and stylesheet evidence separately; show context transitions.
rules.exceptions: Intentional theme or context changes are explained, not suppressed.

rules.title: Structure before appearance
rules.statement: Preserve headings, labels, legends and table relationships when restyling. Visual weight alone is not a structural role.
rules.check: Inspect structure and relationships alongside computed styling.
rules.exceptions: A component redesign may change structure with explicit review.

rules.title: Importance and emphasis
rules.statement: Use strong for importance or urgency, and em for stress emphasis. Choose meaning before its appearance.
rules.check: Review the intended meaning; do not infer it from font weight or italics.
rules.exceptions: Other HTML elements have distinct meanings; do not replace b or i indiscriminately.

rules.title: Labels are components
rules.statement: Style labels through the label component. Do not add strong merely to obtain a heavier label.
rules.check: Compare matching label variants; verify association with the control.
rules.exceptions: Required, optional, checkbox and composite labels can have different documented variants.

rules.title: References survive updates
rules.statement: Retain working, unambiguous naming, description and error references after AJAX updates.
rules.check: Resolve ordered ID references; distinguish generated-ID changes from broken relationships.
rules.exceptions: Matching hashes do not establish identical full accessible names.

rules.title: Consistent interface language
rules.statement: Use sentence case for ordinary interface headings and labels; retain proper names. Keep help separate from labels.
rules.check: Review text in context and against the published UI wording guidance.
rules.exceptions: Translation, proper nouns and established product names need language-aware review.

rules.title: Reuse roles, not copied values
rules.statement: Use the existing component and token system before introducing another spacing, type or colour value.
rules.check: Trace a computed value to its token, library and selector before proposing an override.
rules.exceptions: A deliberate component variant can justify a new token. Token names below are illustrative, not shipped CSS variables.

rules.title: Colour has an explicit purpose
rules.statement: Map foreground, surface, boundary and state roles together. Do not assign meaning from a palette swatch alone.
rules.check: Review actual rendered pairs, simultaneous states and a non-colour cue.
rules.exceptions: Decorative colours need no state meaning. Existing colour-only failures are recorded rather than legitimized.

rules.title: Check actual contrast pairs
rules.statement: Apply WCAG text contrast requirements to actual foreground/background pairs, including their exceptions.
rules.check: Use 4.5:1 for ordinary text and 3:1 for qualifying large text; inspect alpha, images and gradients.
rules.exceptions: Do not turn the exceptions into blanket permission to make disabled information unreadable.

rules.title: Boundaries and indicators remain visible
rules.statement: Review the contrast of necessary control boundaries, state indicators and meaningful graphics.
rules.check: Apply SC 1.4.11 in context, including its 3:1 requirement and exceptions.
rules.exceptions: Not every decorative border is necessary to identify a control.

rules.title: Preferences are independent
rules.statement: Record colour scheme, forced colours, prefers-contrast and theme settings separately.
rules.check: Test individual preferences and useful combinations; retain unsupported values as unknown.
rules.exceptions: A site setting may deliberately override a browser preference; document its precedence.

rules.title: Distinguish simultaneous states
rules.statement: Keep selected, invalid, focused and disabled states distinguishable when they occur together, including forced colours.
rules.check: Review text, shape, boundaries and keyboard focus in each combined state.
rules.exceptions: A double border in a local issue patch is not an accepted global Drupal design rule.

rules.title: Motion must have an alternative
rules.statement: When motion communicates progress or the next action, retain an understandable static cue under reduced motion.
rules.check: Trigger the behaviour in both modes and review completion, orientation and feedback.
rules.exceptions: Essential motion needs a documented rationale. SC 2.3.3 is AAA, not a blanket AA ban on animation.

rules.title: Review residual transitions
rules.statement: Review remaining motion by property and purpose, not just duration or count.
rules.check: Separate declared transitions, observed animation and smooth scrolling. Trigger hover, focus, expand and validation states.
rules.exceptions: A short colour fade is not automatically equivalent to spatial movement or an accessibility failure.

rules.title: Layout preserves task access
rules.statement: Keep content and focused controls usable under narrow widths, text expansion and persistent navigation.
rules.check: Check overlap, clipping, wrapping, zoom and keyboard access, including AJAX states.
rules.exceptions: Geometry intersections alone do not establish obscuration.

rules.title: Action hierarchy matches purpose
rules.statement: Use buttons for actions and links for navigation; select a primary action deliberately.
rules.check: Review element behaviour, label and hierarchy against the task.
rules.exceptions: Wizard controls and component patterns need contextual review.

rules.title: Grouping conveys relationships
rules.statement: Use semantic grouping for related fields and disclosure patterns for optional detail.
rules.check: Review grouping, naming, expanded state and access to invalid fields.
rules.exceptions: Do not convert older numerical limits or collapse recommendations into universal automated failures.

rules.title: Tables remain understandable
rules.statement: Retain identifiable column headers, row operations and sort state, including empty and dynamic tables.
rules.check: Review structural relationships and keyboard interaction after insertion, removal and filtering.
rules.exceptions: A visually empty utility header is a review question, not an automatic defect.

rules.title: Messages explain the outcome
rules.statement: Make error, warning, success and progress messages distinguishable through words and semantics as well as colour.
rules.check: Review placement, field relationships, announcement behaviour and the next action.
rules.exceptions: Live announcements and focus movement need explicit scenarios; an initial-load crawl does not verify them.

rules.title: Declare what printing preserves
rules.statement: For each page family, identify essential content, useful context and interactive chrome that may be omitted.
rules.check: Check inclusion, removal and restyling separately. Keep the reason for each omission.
rules.exceptions: Do not hide every nav, aside, button or form element globally; some are part of the document.

rules.title: Paper layout must not cover content
rules.statement: Prevent navigation, sticky panels and editor sidebars from covering or clipping printed content.
rules.check: Inspect paper-width layout and exported pages. Browser-viewport rectangles are supporting evidence only.
rules.exceptions: An intentional repeated header is acceptable if it does not obscure content.

rules.title: Validate pagination and appearance
rules.statement: Review page breaks, repeated headers, blank trailing sheets and meaning with backgrounds disabled.
rules.check: Inspect A4 and Letter, long tables, expanded detail and monochrome appearance.
rules.exceptions: A PDF file existing, or matching page counts, does not establish quality or accessible PDF structure.

rules.title: Separate editor UI and content
rules.statement: Review editor controls, editable content and saved frontend output as separate styling contexts.
rules.check: Record region, text format, editor version and owning stylesheet before overriding a difference.
rules.exceptions: Editor chrome can legitimately differ from the admin theme; changes need component-level validation.

rules.title: Formatting retains meaning
rules.statement: Verify that allowed formatting produces the intended markup and survives saving and rendering.
rules.check: Use explicit test content and editor actions; compare editor content with the saved frontend result.
rules.exceptions: Text-format filtering and content-theme overrides can intentionally change the allowed output. Current captures did not test this.

rules.title: Adapt without changing intent
rules.statement: Review translated text, direction and regional variants with the same component intent.
rules.check: Test language negotiation, logical directions, wrapping and state indicators in RTL and LTR.
rules.exceptions: Different fonts, strings and dimensions are expected; compare roles and behaviour, not identical pixels.

rules.title: Exceptions are reviewable
rules.statement: Record intentional differences with rule ID, scope, owner, rationale, evidence and review condition.
rules.check: Compare exceptions and baseline identities before classifying a new finding.
rules.exceptions: Do not use a broad theme exception to suppress unrelated component or semantic failures.
